brief.headline: SK Hynix P/E flips Samsung for first time; HBM4 16L pull-in, DRAM +60% Q2, CoWoS 90% CAGR through '27
brief.summary: <cite index="49-1,49-22">SK Hynix's 2026 forward P/E reached 6.79× versus Samsung's 6.77×, the first-ever inversion after a 2.8-point gap three months ago.</cite> <cite index="11-1,14-1">Conventional DRAM contract prices are projected to rise 58–63% QoQ in Q2 2026, while NAND climbs 70–75%, following Q1's record 90–95% DRAM surge.</cite> <cite index="1-12,1-16">Nvidia asked suppliers whether they could deliver 16-layer HBM by Q4 2026, pulling forward the generational transition before 12-layer HBM4 reaches full commercial rollout.</cite> <cite index="31-10,40-9">TSMC is expanding CoWoS capacity at a 90% annual CAGR from 2022 to 2027, scaling from ~35k wafers/month in late 2024 to 130k by close of 2026.</cite> <cite index="29-1,29-6">Hyperscaler 2026 capex estimates now stand at $725bn, nearly double mid-2025 consensus.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: Long SK Hynix / short Samsung. <cite index="3-11,3-17">SK maintains 62% HBM shipment share (Q2 2025) and 57% revenue share (Q3); UBS forecasts ~70% of HBM4 for Nvidia Rubin in 2026.</cite> <cite index="1-22,1-23">Samsung received favorable feedback in Nvidia HBM4 SiP tests, but SK already has mass production framework and paid samples flowing.</cite> <cite index="41-15,41-16,41-17">Samsung union announced 18-day walkout May 21–June 7; KB estimates disruption of 3–4% global DRAM and 2–3% NAND, ~₩1tn/day losses, risking key clients including Nvidia.</cite> <cite index="47-25">Over 200 Samsung engineers defected to SK Hynix in past four months, drawn by uncapped 10% operating-profit bonus pool.</cite> Samsung trades at relative discount (forward P/E now in-line) with materially higher execution risk and labor overhang through mid-June. Tactical window closes if strike averted or Samsung HBM4 qual accelerates H2.

memory_cycle.stage: Mid-upcycle acceleration, supply sold out through 2026
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="14-9">$755bn hyperscaler 2026 capex with memory consuming ~30% is a structural demand floor absent in prior cycles.</cite> <cite index="14-6,14-12,14-13">Memory producers have rational incentive to prioritize HBM over conventional DRAM; AI infrastructure has sold out 2026, no relief before H2 2027.</cite> <cite index="47-16,47-17">SK Hynix entire portfolio (DRAM/NAND/HBM) fully sold out; Goldman raised DRAM supply gap forecast from 3.3% to 4.9%, tightest in 15 years.</cite> <cite index="4-2,4-12">HBM3E supply tight as Samsung/SK prioritize ramping HBM4; both planning ~20% HBM3E price hike for 2026.</cite> Pricing power shifted decisively to suppliers; spot DRAM/NAND inversions signal allocation exhaustion, not cyclical shortage.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-11,1-12,1-13">Nvidia signaled interest in 16-layer HBM for Q4 2026 delivery; discussions exploratory, no contracts, but triggered internal planning on schedules and yields.</cite> <cite index="1-1,3-9">HBM3E will account for 66–67% of total HBM output in 2026 (LS Securities/consensus), down from 87% in 2025 but still dominant.</cite> <cite index="1-8,1-9">Rubin, Nvidia's next-gen AI accelerator launching H2 2026, expected to use eight HBM4 stacks.</cite> <cite index="1-3,1-4,1-6">Samsung considering hybrid bonding for 7th-gen 16L HBM4E due to adhesive-tech lag; SK pacing hybrid as backup while maximizing MR-MUF for current gen.</cite> <cite index="4-5,4-8,4-10">HBM3E demand exceeded expectations post-H200 China export approval (six stacks/chip); Google TPU v7 uses eight HBM3E stacks, Amazon Trainium3 four stacks.</cite> <cite index="2-24,2-25">SK Hynix preparing custom HBM4E for H2 2026 using TSMC 12nm for server-grade base dies, 3nm for Nvidia/Google top-end.</cite> 16-layer pull-in compresses HBM4 → HBM4E window; supply already oversubscribed.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix forward P/E overtakes Samsung for first time at 6.79× vs 6.77×
news_pulse.implication: Structural re-rating: SK now priced as growth story, not cyclical. Valuation convergence limits further relative outperformance but validates margin/share durability.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung union sets 18-day strike May 21–June 7; KB sees 3–4% DRAM supply hit, ₩1tn/day loss
news_pulse.implication: Material production risk in tightest supply environment in 15 years. Any output disruption redirects orders to SK Hynix; Nvidia client loss would be catastrophic for Samsung HBM4 ramp.

news_pulse.headline: Q2 2026 DRAM contract +58–63% QoQ, NAND +70–75%; follows Q1 record +90–95% DRAM surge
news_pulse.implication: NAND outpacing DRAM for first time signals enterprise SSD capacity exhaustion. Deceleration in DRAM rate-of-change (from 90% to 60%) still extreme; no ceiling visible until new capacity H2 '27.

news_pulse.headline: Nvidia asks suppliers for 16-layer HBM delivery Q4 2026; testing expected before Q3
news_pulse.implication: Pulls HBM roadmap forward before 12L HBM4 matures. Samsung/SK/Micron forced into parallel 12L + 16L development; yield/cost pressures intensify. Widens execution gap vs laggards.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex revised to $725bn, nearly double mid-2025 estimates; memory ~30% of total
news_pulse.implication: Sustained demand floor through 2027; capex rising faster than operating cash flow forces debt funding but validates multi-year memory upcycle thesis.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC expanding CoWoS at 90% CAGR '22–'27; capacity 35k→130k wafers/month by end-2026
news_pulse.implication: Alleviates but doesn't eliminate packaging bottleneck. Nvidia holds >60% of '25–'26 capacity; AMD/Broadcom split remainder. CoWoS remains gating item for AI accelerator supply through '27.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung/SK Hynix now 42.2% of KOSPI in May, up from 38.7% YTD start; index hit record
news_pulse.implication: Concentration risk amplifies volatility; any memory correction drags index. But reflects genuine earnings power, not speculative froth—KOSPI +80% YTD mirrors profit reality.

news_pulse.headline: U.S. Roundhill DRAM ETF drew $6bn in first month; Samsung 20%, SK 26% of holdings
news_pulse.implication: Retail capital inflow into memory pure-plays; 2× leveraged SK Hynix ETF launching this month adds technical fuel. Raises stakes for any near-term disappointment.

brief.derivatives_signal: No options data in payload. ADRs (SSNLF, HXSCL) illiquid; use Korea-listed for hedging. Samsung 18-day strike window (May 21–Jun 7) creates binary event vol; structure call spreads around ₩300k if strike averted or put spreads ₩260–280k if production hit materializes. SK Hynix RSI 68.9, extended but not overbought in context of structural re-rating; trailing stop ₩1.85m protects gains while allowing ₩2m breakout. Pair: long SK ₩1.97m / short Samsung ₩284k, stop if Samsung <₩270k (strike resolved favorably) or SK <₩1.80m (HBM share-loss catalyst).
watch_for_next_3h: Samsung union/management back-channel talks through May 20; any settlement headline pre-strike rerates Samsung +5–8% and compresses SK relative premium
Nvidia HBM4 qualification updates (Samsung SiP test results, SK Hynix paid-sample feedback); 16-layer feasibility commentary from supply chain
China response to Trump-Xi summit (May 13–14); semiconductor export-control easing would pressure memory ASPs but broaden TAM—net neutral to slight negative
TSMC CoWoS allocation rumors for Rubin; any indication of Samsung foundry gaining packaging share (I-Cube alternative) shifts competitive landscape
TrendForce/DRAMeXchange Q3 2026 pricing forecast revision (due late May); current trajectory implies +30–40% QoQ but risk of moderation if PC/smartphone demand craters under cost pressure
